frequency_question: How often have congressional resolutions to block major executive-branch nuclear or arms agreements successfully passed both chambers and become law despite executive opposition?
membership_rule: Includes any formal 123 nuclear cooperation agreement or major foreign arms sale submitted to the U.S. Congress for a statutory review period where a resolution of disapproval was introduced. Excludes agreements that were withdrawn prior to a vote or where no formal resolution of disapproval reached floor votes in both chambers.
window: Statutory review periods ranging from 30 to 90 continuous session days.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named cases representing the complete set of major legislative challenges to executive Middle East defense and nuclear agreements of comparable scale.
known_gaps: Sample size is small because successful nuclear cooperation agreements rarely face unified bipartisan overrides of executive vetoes.
skeleton: Named historical instances of congressional attempts to block major executive Middle East security/nuclear agreements via joint resolutions of disapproval.
validity_reason: Institutional veto dynamics and statutory thresholds (requiring a two-thirds majority in both houses to override a veto) remain stable across decades.
